schemes.module_code: ISYE 4106 (per search result; page itself gives no number)
schemes.description: Capstone for ISyE undergraduate seniors: teams of about six (example) take a real organisational need from a published client listing, supervised by a faculty advisor, producing a design with economic analysis, presentations and a written report delivered to the client. Clients are mostly external companies, hospitals and public bodies; a minority of listed projects are for internal Georgia Tech units.
schemes.admin_host: H. Milton Stewart School of Industrial and Systems Engineering
schemes.year_of_study: Senior (preceded by a pre-senior design semester)
schemes.credit_assessment: Course credit not stated on fetched page; each member at least 12 productive hours/week (180 hours/semester)
schemes.duration: Pre-senior design semester plus senior design semester
schemes.project_evidence: Requirements: engineering design with economic analysis; deliverables incl. proposal, interim and final presentations and written report [1].
schemes.group_evidence: Undergraduate student teams (six-member example), team formed in pre-senior semester, joint work products [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Client identifies need, meets team on site, assigns a contact spending c.2-4 hours/week with the team supplying guidance, data and site access, and receives proposal, interim report and final design/written report [1]. Spring 2027 listing: 38 projects from 29 clients incl. Google, Coca-Cola, Accenture, Emory Healthcare, American Airlines, Wellstar, Housing Authority of the City of Atlanta; a minority of listings are internal GT units (e.g. GT Strategic Consulting, Parking and Transportation Services, Registrar). Internal share is a minority; external clients are the documented norm [1].
schemes.partner_role: Client: identifies need, provides data/site/contact, receives report and presentations (internal Georgia Tech units are a minority of clients and are not counted as external)
schemes.named_partners: Spring 2027 listing: Google, Coca-Cola, Accenture, Emory Healthcare, American Airlines, Novelis, Wellstar Health System, Waffle House, Housing Authority of the City of Atlanta (page lists 29 clients)
schemes.deliverable: Design/recommendation report and presentations to client
schemes.latest_evidenced_year: 2026/27 (Spring 2027 project listing; Spring 2026 finalists luncheon news 13 May 2026)
schemes.participation_data: 29 teams completed senior design in Spring 2025 (search-result summary of ISyE capstone site); 38 projects listed for Spring 2027
schemes.unresolved: Course credit hours; the 'compulsory' statement rests on the page calling it the capstone for all ISyE undergraduate seniors.

schemes.official_name: Capstone Design (Institute-wide course and Capstone Design Expo)

schemes.description: Semester-long senior capstone in which teams (about five graduating seniors, often interdisciplinary) work on sponsor-proposed design challenges and present at the Capstone Design Expo. Spring 2025 Expo: 238 teams, 1,300+ students, projects across 12 disciplines in four colleges; almost 60% of teams worked on industry-sponsored projects, the rest on other (research, student-proposed, or start-up) projects.
schemes.admin_host: Center for Engineering Design, Entrepreneurship and Innovation / College of Engineering departments
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Undergraduates in BME, CEE, ECE, ISyE, MSE, ME, public policy and multidisciplinary teams (also computing, design, architecture, liberal arts per news)
schemes.project_evidence: Semester-long design projects with prototypes and reports [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: Team of 5 graduating seniors per sponsor; example teams of five to eight [1][2].
schemes.employer_evidence: Sponsors propose the problem, fund the course, usually receive report and prototype and may judge the Expo [2], but only almost 60% of Spring 2025 teams were industry-sponsored [1] and ECE says teams 'may' take on an industry challenge or build research tools/start-ups [3]. External sponsorship is not universal, so C is Unclear for the course as a whole.

schemes.named_partners: Emory Healthcare surgeon-proposed retractor (Spring 2025); restor3d (Spring 2024, per search result)

schemes.unresolved: No 2025/26 or 2026/27 dated source; which departments mandate sponsor projects; ECE Senior Design recorded here rather than separately.

profile_md: Georgia Tech's strongest verified route is ISyE Senior Design, a compulsory seniors' capstone in which teams of about six solve a real problem for an external client (38 Spring 2027 projects from 29 clients; Spring 2026 cohort reported in May 2026 news). The client assigns a contact, gives data and site access, and receives a report and presentations. A minority of listed clients are internal Georgia Tech units. The institute-wide Capstone Design course and Expo (Spring 2025: 238 teams, 1,300+ students, roughly 60% industry-sponsored) shows the same model across engineering, with some computing, design and policy students, but the remaining teams have research, student or non-industry briefs, so employer connection is recorded as unclear. The BS Public Policy Policy Task Force (PUBP 4010/4020) is a required two-semester team capstone with agency, non-profit or company clients who evaluate reports, but the page is undated. Scheller's Pro Bono Consulting and MBA practicums are graduate team client projects, also undated. VIP is a university-level multisemester team programme, but it is faculty-research-led with optional industry sponsorship. CS Capstone clients may be internal or external. No College of Sciences route was found.
gaps: Further departmental capstones (ME, ECE, CEE, BME, MSE) likely follow the sponsor model but were not individually verified. SLS course partnerships, Design studios, INTA 4744 and MS SCE capstone were not opened. Undated pages (PUBP, Pro Bono, MBA practicums) lack current-delivery corroboration. No participation data except ISyE and Expo counts. Retrieval was via WebFetch summaries (not verbatim) and search summaries.
